# Per the proxy's own documentation a 403/407 is an organisation egress-policy denial and is
# NOT to be retried or routed around. It was not. No host was probed twice.
## 🔴 THE CHANNEL ASYMMETRY HAS INVERTED ITS AXIS, AND THAT IS THE FINDING
# p189 found: CODE at primary fidelity, REGULATION at secondary fidelity.
# p190 finds a SECOND, orthogonal split, and it cuts code in half:
#   🟢 READING named code  : FULL fidelity. Any repository whose slug is already known can be
#      cloned and read byte for byte. This pass read 33 tool definitions, 4 rails modules, a
#      Django admin and a licence corpus that way.
#   🔴 DISCOVERING code    : GONE. Topics, repository search, trending, star counts and
#      commit dates all live on github.com HTML or the API. Both are 403.
# 🔵 So p190 could not have been a breadth pass whatever it intended. It could only be a
# DEPTH pass — and the six actions p189 pre-registered were all depth actions, which is the
# only reason the pass has a result at all.
## 🔴 THE METHOD LESSON, AND IT IS SHARPER THAN p189's
# p189 RETIRED the absent rate (it measured this KB's own backlog) and PROMOTED the
# new-supply rate to be the published coverage measure — on ONE measurement, over a channel
# that was gone ONE PASS LATER.
# 🟢 RULE: a figure is not a published measure until its CHANNEL has survived more than one
# pass. p189's rule was "ask what would have to be true for the number to move". p190 adds
# the prior question: ask whether you will still be able to ASK. A measure whose channel is
# one policy change from disappearing is a reading, not a measure.
# 🔴 CONSEQUENCE: this KB currently has NO published coverage measure. The absent rate is
# retired and the new-supply rate has exactly one measurement (p189: 12 new slugs, 83%
# absent, 239 rows). Quote it as "one measurement, 2026-10-14, p189", with the channel named,
# or quote nothing. Do NOT present it as a rate.
## 🟢 ONE CHANNEL SUBSTITUTION THAT DID WORK, recorded for p191
# Web search CAN reach github.com content that direct HTTP cannot — it returned repository
# titles, star counts and "last updated" dates for github.com/topics/ai-education while
# curl on the same URL returned 403.
# 🔴 But it is SECONDARY fidelity for exactly the fields this KB verifies: a star count or a
# commit date from a search snippet is a quotation of a page nobody here read.
# 🟢 USE IT FOR DISCOVERY ONLY — to obtain SLUGS. Then verify every slug over git/raw, which
# is primary and open. That is the only sound composition of the two channels, and it is how
# the three DeepTutor / Open-TutorAI licence rows in this pass were produced: slug from
# search, bytes from raw.
